trails.title: Friendly Exchange
trails.description: A crumpled note is attached to the door, its edges torn and folded, emphasizing the messenger's urgent need to communicate.

content.text:
Listen, I've had enough of you playing with the mirrors, you d**n noisy green bird! Stop bringing in any old quack, peddler, or foreigner off the street! And those horrible, unbearable noises—the mirrors that could practically blind someone! I'm not a fool, you daft green parrot! If you're going to call it a wand, it should look like a stick, not a mirror! I really don't want to see those d**n blue striped pants anymore!

    —Those d**n mirrors!

    If you don't learn to behave yourself and control your "patients," you'll be getting a lot more from me than just a piece of paper next time!

    Now go back to your nouveau riche cliques and stop causing trouble here!

trails.title: Trail ① The Shadow in the Broken Mirror
trails.description: A hint of mystery lingers in the air, like a pleasant dream that refuses to fade from memory.

items.text: Between the Doors

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Phew. The reflections she created were real enough, but not perfect.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: The reflections had neither shadows nor breath. Most importantly, they didn't have her passion and subtle movements.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I "read" the truth from these details ... She meant me no harm. Maybe it was just a little trick she was playing.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But, I ...
She steadies her breath, looking down at the figure on the ground.
She inadvertently used too much force. Kakania is still on the ground, supporting her hat with one hand.
Her lips tremble incredulously, shocked by her own failure.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: This is ... That was ...
She lunges toward Marcus, who reflexively withdraws her hand.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I knew it! Your arcane skill is incredibly unique, you can discover what's on the inside by observing what's on the outside.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You are born to be a psychiatrist!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Huh?
She clings tightly to Marcus's hand, as if she's found a long-lost relative.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Look at you, you are so tiny, and they gave you this big coat. How can they do this to a child?!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: How about you quit the Foundation and be my assistant? Your perception would be invaluable in this line of work. After all, we search for truth from foggy memories and vague descriptions for a living ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ah, Miss ... The book ...
Marcus attempts to withdraw her hand, politely but stiffly.
Kakania's enthusiasm remains unchanged.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Forget the book! A new academic field is opening its doors to you! Let's go inside. Oh dear, I forgot your tea!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Gosh, she's babbling like a parrot.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ah ...! It's Madam Hofmann!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ma'am.

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Marcus, the "Spider Tail" has shown me your direction. How did you get that far? What is that place? An arcane fluctuation?!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I'm with the targe- ... Ms. Kakania. In her clinic. I'm safe, the investigation's going well! Ma'am!

items.speaker: Hofmann
items.text: Stay where you are, I'm on my way! And take care of yourself, you hear me?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Erm, yes, ma'am ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Was that your supervisor? She sounds rather harsh. I do have to question the Foundation, hiring underage children and all ...

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: ... Just in time!
Marcus glances at the doctor, who is now lost in thought, lightly flicking her skirt. An almost invisible thread lands on the green fabric.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Well, actually, Madam Hofmann is ... very kind to me.
She lifts her head, trying to further divert the doctor's attention.
Kakania remains unimpressed by her answer.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Well, you have seen it all for yourself. Me, my clinic, my arcane skill—I showed you everything. Have they cleared up your doubts, Ms. Marcus?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Just one more question.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Please go ahead.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: About ... "The Circle."

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Eh? Did you go through all this trouble just for that?
Kakania dramatically raises her hand, settling down into her soft chair.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You could have asked me earlier. I am the founder of "The Circle."

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Wh-what?!
Marcus nearly scalds herself with the hot tea as she brings it up to her lips.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You're awfully excited. Are you an admirer?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Joking. It's just a little group a couple of friends started out of interest. Completely legal, nothing nefarious.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We're committed to changing the arcanists' current situation ... more committed than the Foundation.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: There will be a non-profit exhibit soon, and all donations will help lower class arcanists get their license, which should have been your responsibility!
Her words are sharply pointed, only to stop abruptly as she recalls the identity of their target.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, sorry, I get carried away. I should persuade you to join us, not attack your current job.
Marcus shakes her head, feeling all-together fortunate now to not be involved in the disputes of this era.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: And the painting in this exhibit ... will be The Salvation?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That's right, you've been to the Secession Building, and that's a masterpiece which will be hard to miss.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: That was Theophil's final piece of work, the Golden Isle being its subject.
She lowers her head a little while refilling her cup with fresh tea.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It was big news at the time ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The island hidden from all people in the Aegean Sea, the ancient arcanist settlement, the strange current and magnetic field around it, the animals only heard in stories, and the shadow of modern society cast upon it ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Well, those are just hearsay. People have all kinds of speculations about it ... A military base, a mythical kingdom, the apocalypse ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The Foundation knows it better than any of us.
*clink*
Kakania sets down the teacup, her focus calm but impassioned.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ms. Marcus, I've told you everything I know. If you trust me, please tell me one thing.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I'm sorry, Ms. Kakania, I can't ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Are there really our people on that island? If so, how did they protect themselves in these changing times?

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: This is my only question. As an arcanist, and as a human being.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: The arms companies are turning the Balkan Peninsula into a proving ground for their new weapons—that was how they discovered this island.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: You work for the authorities. You must know something. Please, I just want to know if ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: If there's any more of us in this world, suffering, silenced, and helpless.
Kakania's passion dims over the prolonged silence.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Fine. You work for the Foundation, after all. I shouldn't have asked.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It's just that I'm hoping for at least one rational person in such an irredeemable bureaucracy. Someone who doesn't think it's just a bunch of deranged lunatics over there.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: ... Which is a stigma the arcanists have carried around for centuries.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: … No, we are not crazy!
She clenches the fabric of her dress, lifting her head in a trembling outburst.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: I, I don't think the arcanists on the island are crazy either!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Ms. Marcus?

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Dr. Kakania, I know there has been discord and resentment between humans and arcanists, but not everyone is like Mr. Karl.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: We're from the headquarters, where many like you are fighting for the rights of arcanists.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: When it comes to caring for our people, we're not so different there.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That was what the Foundation was for. To defend the interests of the arcanists, and to keep the world safe and orderly. Till this day, we continue to strive for this goal.
Her heart thumps hard in her chest.
She shouldn't do this ... but, but, she can't ignore the question any longer either.
Perhaps it's worth it! Her "reading" tells her that this is a worthwhile ally. They have had no fundamental disagreements between one another.
Just this one insignificant piece of information ... if it might bridge the gap in their positions ...
Time stretches on.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: My sympathies for all that is happening.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Erm?!
Marcus receives another embrace.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We could've been very good friends, if you weren't working for the Foundation.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I know you meant every word you said, I can see how you burned with passion. "The Circle" was founded for the same reason.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But I will not change my view on certain things.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Ah ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: But on second thought, I have friends working in all kinds of places ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: We have a big house, plenty of wine and refreshments, there is more than enough room for a new friend.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I would like to invite you to the Secession Building and to be present at the opening of the exhibit, Ms. Marcus.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: And we can talk more about what you said afterwards.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: That'd be great!

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: But ... my ment- ... um, my supervisor ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Hmm, that is tricky. But a minor like you requires the presence of a guardian, and you told me that she's "kind" to you ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Well, she can come with you. We must abide by the law, after all.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: It might help to clear up misunderstandings if she's there.
A hug comes once again.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Alright, I have to inform Heinrich that we have two more guests coming ...

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Oh, shoot!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I have an appointment today! I almost forgot the time. I have to go. I know what you're going to ask, but patient information is confidential!
Kakania idly wags her finger. Her thoughts seem to have drifted on to future treatments.
She hastily caps her pen, handing the invitation to Marcus.

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: I shouldn't keep you any longer. See you soon, Ms. Foundation!

items.speaker: Kakania
items.text: Welcome to "The Circle!"
A gentle knock sounds at the door.

items.speaker: Marcus
items.text: Oh, I, I should go ... Thank you, Ms. Kakania.
She turns and hurries away, the door opening just in time.
Marcus doesn't stop, nodding and gliding around the newcomer in a fast, fluid motion.
TO BE CONTINUED…
